question: If you have a manual transmission vehicle, what should you do before taking your right foot off the brake when starting, to avoid rolling back?
choice_a: Shift into neutral
choice_b: Partly engage the clutch
choice_c: Apply full throttle immediately
choice_d: Release the parking brake first
explanation: The Idaho manual instructs drivers with a manual transmission to partly engage the clutch before taking the right foot off the brake, and to apply the parking brake whenever necessary to keep from rolling back.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2.1 Accelerating

question: According to the Idaho manual, if your drive wheels begin to spin because of poor traction while accelerating, what should you do?
choice_a: Press the accelerator harder
choice_b: Shift into a higher gear
choice_c: Take your foot off the accelerator
choice_d: Apply the parking brake
explanation: The manual states that if you use too much power on poor traction you could lose control, so if the drive wheels begin to spin, you should take your foot off the accelerator.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2.1 Accelerating

question: How does the Idaho manual say you should hold the steering wheel while driving?
choice_a: Loosely, so you can react quickly
choice_b: With one hand on the wheel and one on the gearshift
choice_c: Firmly, with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel
choice_d: With both hands close together at the top of the wheel
explanation: The manual instructs holding the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides, because if you hit a curb or pothole, the wheel could pull away from your hands unless you have a firm hold.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2.2 Steering

question: Why does the Idaho manual say you should avoid backing whenever you can and try to park so you can pull forward when you leave?
choice_a: It saves fuel
choice_b: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle
choice_c: It is illegal in most parking lots
choice_d: It reduces wear on the transmission
explanation: The manual states that because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle, backing is always dangerous, so you should avoid backing whenever you can and try to park so you can pull forward when leaving.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2.4 Backing Safely

question: According to the Idaho manual, why should you back and turn toward the driver's side whenever possible?
choice_a: It is required by state law
choice_b: It allows you to watch the rear of your vehicle by looking out the side window
choice_c: It puts less strain on the drivetrain
choice_d: It is faster than backing to the right
explanation: The manual explains that backing toward the right side is very dangerous because you can't see as well, while backing and turning toward the driver's side lets you watch the rear of your vehicle by looking out the side window.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2.4 Backing Safely

question: What does the Idaho manual recommend regarding gear and speed when backing?
choice_a: Back as slowly as possible, using the lowest reverse gear
choice_b: Back at normal driving speed to avoid stalling
choice_c: Use a middle reverse gear for the best control
choice_d: Coast in neutral while backing
explanation: The manual advises backing as slowly as possible using the lowest reverse gear, so you can more easily correct steering errors and stop quickly if necessary.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2.4 Backing Safely

question: Before backing with the help of another person, what does the Idaho manual say the driver and helper should agree on?
choice_a: Which side mirror to use
choice_b: A set of hand signals, including a signal for "stop"
choice_c: The exact backing speed in miles per hour
choice_d: Who is responsible if a collision occurs
explanation: The manual states that before you begin backing, you should work out a set of hand signals that both the driver and helper understand, and agree on a signal for "stop."
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2.4 Backing Safely

question: According to the Idaho manual, what do most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require to change gears?
choice_a: Double clutching
choice_b: A single quick clutch press
choice_c: No clutch use at all
choice_d: Shifting only while stationary
explanation: The manual states that most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to change gears.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.3.1 Manual Transmissions

question: The Idaho manual lists two special conditions where you should downshift. What are they?
choice_a: Before merging and before parking
choice_b: Before accelerating and before signaling
choice_c: Before starting down a hill and before entering a curve
choice_d: Before fueling and before an inspection
explanation: The manual identifies downshifting before starting down a hill and before entering a curve as the two special conditions where you should downshift.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.3.1 Manual Transmissions

question: Why does the Idaho manual say you should downshift and slow down before starting down a hill?
choice_a: So you shift to a speed you can control without using the brakes hard, since brakes can overheat and lose braking power
choice_b: So the engine idles more smoothly
choice_c: To reduce tire wear on the downgrade
choice_d: So you can use the horn more effectively
explanation: The manual explains that downshifting before a hill lets you control your speed without using the brakes hard, since otherwise the brakes can overheat and lose their braking power.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.3.1 Manual Transmissions

question: When should you turn off a vehicle's retarder, according to the Idaho manual?
choice_a: Whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered
choice_b: Whenever driving downhill
choice_c: Only at night
choice_d: Whenever the vehicle is fully loaded
explanation: The manual cautions that when your drive wheels have poor traction, a retarder may cause them to skid, so you should turn the retarder off whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.3.4 Retarders

question: According to the Idaho manual, how far ahead do most good drivers look while driving?
choice_a: 2 to 3 seconds
choice_b: 12 to 15 seconds
choice_c: 30 to 45 seconds
choice_d: 5 to 8 seconds
explanation: The manual states that most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead, which is about one block at lower speeds and about a quarter mile at highway speeds.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.4.1 Seeing Ahead

topic: Seeing to the Sides and Rear
question: According to the Idaho manual, when should mirror adjustment be checked, and under what condition can it only be accurately checked?
choice_a: Once a year, and only when the vehicle is empty
choice_b: After every fuel stop, and only in daylight
choice_c: Prior to the start of any trip, and only when the trailer(s) are straight
choice_d: Only after an accident, and only when parked
explanation: The manual states mirror adjustment should be checked prior to the start of any trip and can only be checked accurately when the trailer(s) are straight.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.4.2 Seeing to the Sides and Rear

topic: Seeing to the Sides and Rear
question: During a lane change, the Idaho manual lists four separate times to check your mirrors. What are they?
choice_a: Only before signaling and only after completing the change
choice_b: Before changing lanes, after signaling, right after starting the change, and after completing it
choice_c: Only once, immediately before turning the wheel
choice_d: Only when another vehicle honks its horn
explanation: The manual lists checking mirrors before changing lanes, after signaling to check the blind spot, right after starting the lane change, and after completing the lane change.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.4.2 Seeing to the Sides and Rear

question: According to the Idaho manual, what is a key characteristic of convex ("fisheye") mirrors found on many large vehicles?
choice_a: They eliminate blind spots completely
choice_b: They show a wider area, but objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are
choice_c: They only work properly at night
choice_d: They show a narrower area but magnify objects
explanation: The manual explains that convex mirrors show a wider area than flat mirrors, but everything appears smaller and farther away than it really is, so drivers must allow for this.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.4.2 Seeing to the Sides and Rear

question: What three rules for using turn signals does the Idaho manual give?
choice_a: Signal loudly, signal twice, signal only in bad weather
choice_b: Signal after turning, signal briefly, leave it on
choice_c: Signal early, signal continuously, and cancel your signal after you've turned
choice_d: Signal only on highways, use lights only, never hand signals
explanation: The manual gives three rules: signal early to keep others from trying to pass you, signal continuously without canceling until the turn is complete, and cancel your signal after you've turned.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5.1 Signal Your Intentions

question: How does the Idaho manual say you should warn drivers behind you that you will need to slow down?
choice_a: Sound the horn continuously
choice_b: Swerve slightly within your lane
choice_c: A few light taps on the brake pedal, enough to flash the brake lights
choice_d: Turn on your headlights
explanation: The manual advises a few light taps on the brake pedal, enough to flash the brake lights, to warn drivers behind you that you'll need to slow down.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5.1 Signal Your Intentions

question: According to the Idaho manual, when should you use the four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers?
choice_a: For times when you are driving very slowly or are stopped
choice_b: Only when parked in a garage
choice_c: Whenever your headlights are broken
choice_d: Only when directed by a police officer
explanation: The manual states you should use the four-way emergency flashers for times when you are driving very slowly or are stopped, where legal.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5.1 Signal Your Intentions

question: According to the Idaho manual, what should you do when passing a vehicle, pedestrian, or bicyclist, since you should assume they don't see you?
choice_a: Ignore them and maintain your speed and lane position
choice_b: Tap the horn lightly, or at night flash your lights from low to high beam and back, when legal to do so
choice_c: Come to a complete stop until they acknowledge you
choice_d: Swerve into the next lane immediately
explanation: The manual advises that when passing a vehicle, pedestrian, or bicyclist, you should assume they don't see you, and when it is legal, tap the horn lightly or, at night, flash your lights from low to high beam and back.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence

question: What does the Idaho manual warn about using your horn unnecessarily?
choice_a: It can startle others and could be dangerous
choice_b: It has no real effect either way
choice_c: It is required at every intersection
choice_d: It always prevents a crash
explanation: The manual states your horn can help avoid a crash and should be used when needed, but it can startle others and could be dangerous when used unnecessarily.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence

question: If you must stop on a road or shoulder, within how much time does the Idaho manual say you must put out your emergency warning devices?
choice_a: One minute
choice_b: Thirty minutes
choice_c: One hour
choice_d: Ten minutes
explanation: The manual states that if you must stop on a road or the shoulder of any road, you must put out your emergency warning devices within ten minutes.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence

question: If you stop on a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions, where does the Idaho manual say to place your warning devices?
choice_a: 500 feet in front of the vehicle only
choice_b: Directly under the trailer
choice_c: Within 10 feet of the front or rear corners of the vehicle, and 100 feet behind and ahead of the vehicle
choice_d: Only 5 feet behind the vehicle
explanation: The manual instructs placing warning devices within 10 feet of the front or rear corners to mark the vehicle's location, and 100 feet behind and ahead of the vehicle, on a two-lane or undivided road.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence

question: If you must stop on or by a one-way or divided highway, at what distances toward the approaching traffic does the Idaho manual say to place your warning devices?
choice_a: 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet
choice_b: 50 feet, 250 feet, and 500 feet
choice_c: 1 foot, 10 feet, and 20 feet
choice_d: 100 feet, 300 feet, and 600 feet
explanation: The manual states that if you must stop on or by a one-way or divided highway, you should place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward the approaching traffic.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence

question: According to the Idaho manual, what is the average perception time for an alert driver, and how far does the vehicle travel at 55 mph during that time?
choice_a: About 1 3/4 seconds, accounting for about 142 feet
choice_b: About 5 seconds, accounting for about 500 feet
choice_c: About 0.1 second, accounting for about 5 feet
choice_d: About 3 seconds, accounting for about 200 feet
explanation: The manual states the average perception time for an alert driver is 1 3/4 seconds, which at 55 mph accounts for 142 feet traveled from the time your eyes see a hazard until your brain recognizes it.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.1 Stopping Distance

question: The Idaho manual states the average driver's reaction time is what, and how far does the vehicle travel at 55 mph during that time?
choice_a: About 5 seconds, accounting for about 500 feet
choice_b: About 3/4 second to 1 second, accounting for about 61 feet
choice_c: About 0.1 second, accounting for about 5 feet
choice_d: About 3 seconds, accounting for about 200 feet
explanation: The manual states the average driver has a reaction time of 3/4 second to 1 second, which at 55 mph accounts for about 61 feet traveled before the brakes are physically applied.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.1 Stopping Distance

question: At 55 mph on dry pavement with good brakes, about how far does the Idaho manual say braking distance can be?
choice_a: About 50 feet
choice_b: About 419 feet
choice_c: About 216 feet
choice_d: About 1,000 feet
explanation: The manual states that at 55 mph on dry pavement with good brakes, braking distance can take about 216 feet.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.1 Stopping Distance

question: According to the Idaho manual, what is the minimum total stopping distance at 55 mph, combining perception, reaction, and braking distance?
choice_a: About 142 feet
choice_b: About 61 feet
choice_c: About 216 feet
choice_d: About 419 feet
explanation: The manual states that at 55 mph, your vehicle will travel a minimum total stopping distance of 419 feet when perception, reaction, and braking distances are combined.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.1 Stopping Distance

question: According to the Idaho manual, if you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, how much greater is the impact and braking distance?
choice_a: 2 times greater
choice_b: 4 times greater
choice_c: 9 times greater
choice_d: 16 times greater
explanation: The manual explains that doubling speed from 20 to 40 mph makes the impact 4 times greater, and the braking distance is also 4 times longer.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.1 Stopping Distance

question: According to the Idaho manual, if you triple your speed from 20 to 60 mph, and then increase it further to 80 mph, how does the impact and braking distance compare?
choice_a: The impact and braking distance are 9 times greater at 60 mph, and 16 times greater at 80 mph, than at 20 mph
choice_b: The impact and braking distance stay the same regardless of speed
choice_c: The impact and braking distance are only twice as great at any of these speeds
choice_d: The impact and braking distance decrease as speed increases
explanation: The manual states that tripling speed from 20 to 60 mph makes the impact and braking distance 9 times greater, and increasing to 80 mph makes them 16 times greater than at 20 mph.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.1 Stopping Distance

question: Why does the Idaho manual say empty trucks require greater stopping distances than fully loaded ones?
choice_a: Empty trucks always have weaker brakes installed
choice_b: Empty vehicles have less traction, since brakes, tires, springs, and shock absorbers are designed to work best fully loaded
choice_c: Empty trucks are required by law to travel faster
choice_d: Empty trucks have no functioning brake lights
explanation: The manual notes that brakes, tires, springs, and shock absorbers on heavy vehicles are designed to work best when the vehicle is fully loaded, and empty trucks require greater stopping distances because an empty vehicle has less traction.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.1 Stopping Distance

question: About how much should you reduce your speed on a wet road, according to the Idaho manual?
choice_a: About two-thirds
choice_b: About one-tenth
choice_c: You should not change your speed on wet roads
choice_d: About one-third (e.g., from 55 to about 35 mph)
explanation: The manual advises reducing speed by about one-third on a wet road, for example slowing from 55 to about 35 mph, since wet roads can double stopping distance.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.2 Matching Speed to the Road Surface

question: According to the Idaho manual, how much should you reduce your speed on packed snow, and what should you do if the surface is icy?
choice_a: Reduce speed by a half or more on packed snow; on ice, reduce to a crawl and stop driving as soon as you safely can
choice_b: No reduction is necessary on packed snow or ice
choice_c: Reduce speed by only 5 mph on packed snow; ice requires no change
choice_d: Reduce speed by a half on ice, but drive normally on packed snow
explanation: The manual states that on packed snow you should reduce speed by a half, or more, and if the surface is icy, reduce speed to a crawl and stop driving as soon as you can safely do so.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.2 Matching Speed to the Road Surface

question: How does the Idaho manual describe "black ice"?
choice_a: Ice that is always visibly black in color
choice_b: A type of road paint used to mark hazards
choice_c: Ice found only on gravel roads
choice_d: A thin layer of ice clear enough to see the road underneath, making the road look wet
explanation: The manual defines black ice as a thin layer that is clear enough that you can see the road underneath, making the road look wet; watch for it whenever the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.2 Matching Speed to the Road Surface

question: According to the Idaho manual, why should you be especially careful on bridges when the temperature is close to 32 degrees Fahrenheit?
choice_a: Bridges are always closed below freezing
choice_b: Bridges will freeze before the road will
choice_c: Bridges have no traction at any temperature
choice_d: Bridges only ice over in the summer
explanation: The manual states that when the temperature drops, bridges will freeze before the road will, so you should be especially careful when the temperature is close to 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.2 Matching Speed to the Road Surface

question: According to the Idaho manual, hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as what, if there is a lot of water on the road?
choice_a: 10 mph
choice_b: 55 mph
choice_c: 30 mph
choice_d: 70 mph
explanation: The manual states that it does not take a lot of water to cause hydroplaning, and it can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is a lot of water present.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.2 Matching Speed to the Road Surface

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what does the Idaho manual say you should do, and what should you NOT do?
choice_a: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch; do not use the brakes to slow down
choice_b: Press the accelerator harder; do not touch the clutch
choice_c: Apply the brakes firmly; do not release the accelerator
choice_d: Turn the steering wheel sharply; do not release the accelerator
explanation: The manual instructs that you can regain control by releasing the accelerator and pushing in the clutch, letting the wheels turn freely, but if the vehicle is hydroplaning you should not use the brakes to slow down.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.2 Matching Speed to the Road Surface

question: According to the Idaho manual, what must you use as the principal way of controlling speed on downgrades?
choice_a: Rapid, repeated hard braking
choice_b: The parking brake
choice_c: The braking effect of the engine
choice_d: The trailer hand valve only
explanation: The manual states you must use the braking effect of the engine as the principal way of controlling your speed on downgrades, saving your brakes so you'll be able to slow or stop as needed.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.6 Speed on Downgrades

question: What does the Idaho manual identify as the number one cause of injury and death in roadway work zones?
choice_a: Poor lighting
choice_b: Speeding traffic
choice_c: Vehicle breakdowns
choice_d: Improper signage
explanation: The manual states that speeding traffic is the number one cause of injury and death in roadway work zones, so posted speed limits must be observed at all times.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6.7 Roadway Work Zones

question: What following-distance rule does the Idaho manual give for vehicle speeds below 40 mph?
choice_a: A fixed 2 seconds regardless of vehicle length
choice_b: At least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length
choice_c: One car length for every 10 mph of speed
choice_d: At least 5 seconds regardless of vehicle length
explanation: The manual's rule is at least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph, with an additional second added at greater speeds.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7.1 Space Ahead

question: According to the Idaho manual, how many seconds of following distance should a driver of a 60-foot rig leave when traveling above 40 mph?
choice_a: 4 seconds
choice_b: 5 seconds
choice_c: 6 seconds
choice_d: 7 seconds
explanation: The manual's example gives 6 seconds for a 60-foot rig under 40 mph, and states you must add 1 second for speeds above 40 mph, making it 7 seconds.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7.1 Space Ahead

question: According to the Idaho manual, what "tricks" should you avoid if you are being tailgated?
choice_a: Turning on your taillights or flashing your brake lights
choice_b: Increasing your following distance
choice_c: Signaling early before slowing down
choice_d: Avoiding quick changes in speed or direction
explanation: The manual specifically warns to avoid tricks like turning on your taillights or flashing your brake lights to discourage a tailgater, and instead recommends increasing following distance and avoiding quick changes.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7.2 Space Behind

question: Why does the Idaho manual warn against assuming that posted bridge and overpass heights are always correct?
choice_a: Posted heights only apply to buses
choice_b: Bridges are rebuilt every year
choice_c: Re-paving or packed snow may have reduced the clearances since the heights were posted
choice_d: Heights are chosen at random by local governments
explanation: The manual cautions that re-paving or packed snow may have reduced clearances since the heights were posted, and also notes that an empty van is higher than a loaded one.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7.4 Space Overhead

question: When making a right turn in a vehicle that cannot make the turn without swinging into another lane, what does the Idaho manual advise about vehicle position?
choice_a: Straddle both lanes throughout the turn
choice_b: Turn wide as you complete the turn while keeping the rear of the vehicle close to the curb
choice_c: Turn wide to the left as you start the turn
choice_d: Come to a complete stop before beginning any turn
explanation: The manual advises turning wide as you complete the turn while keeping the rear of the vehicle close to the curb, which stops other drivers from passing you on the right.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7.6 Space for Turns

question: On a left turn, what does the Idaho manual advise to avoid hitting another vehicle due to off-tracking?
choice_a: Start the turn from the far-right lane
choice_b: Turn as soon as you enter the intersection
choice_c: Make sure you have reached the center of the intersection before starting the left turn
choice_d: Turn only when a passenger signals it is clear
explanation: The manual warns that if you turn too soon on a left turn, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle because of off-tracking, so make sure you have reached the center of the intersection before you start the turn.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7.6 Space for Turns
